fields.claim_quote: Lemma 1. A non-empty face F of a polyhedron is minimal if and only if F is a single point (i.e., dim(F) = 0).
fields.complete_source:
Solution:
Consider the polyhedron defined by the set {x : Ax ≤b}. If F is a minimal face
of this polyhedron, demonstrate that Ax = Ay for every pair of points x, y ∈F.
Definition 1. Let P = {x : Ax ≤b} be a polyhedron where A ∈Rm×n and b ∈Rm. A face
of P is a set of the form
F = {x ∈P : aT
i x = bi for all i ∈I}
for some index set I ⊆{1, . . . , m}, where aT
i denotes the i-th row of A.
A face is minimal (or an extreme face) if it contains no other proper faces, i.e., if
F ′ ⊆F is a face, then either F ′ = ∅or F ′ = F.
Theorem 1. If F is a minimal face of the polyhedron P = {x : Ax ≤b}, then Ax = Ay for
every pair of points x, y ∈F.
Proof. We first establish a key characterization of minimal faces.
Lemma 1. A non-empty face F of a polyhedron is minimal if and only if F is a single point
(i.e., dim(F) = 0).
Proof of Lemma. (⇐) If F = {v} for some point v, then the only faces contained in F are
∅and F itself. Thus F is minimal.
(⇒) Suppose F is a minimal non-empty face with dim(F) ≥1. Then F contains at least
two distinct points x, y. Consider the line segment [x, y] = {λx+(1−λ)y : λ ∈[0, 1]}. Since
F is convex and contains x, y, we have [x, y] ⊆F.
For any point w in the relative interior of [x, y] (i.e., w = λx + (1 −λ)y with λ ∈(0, 1)),
the set {w} can be expressed as a face obtained by maximizing an appropriately chosen
linear functional over F. Specifically, there exists a vector c such that {w} = {z ∈F : cTz =
maxu∈F cTu}.
This contradicts the minimality of F, as {w} is a proper face of F. Therefore, dim(F) =
0.
Main Proof:
Since F is a minimal face, by the lemma, F = {v} for some point v ∈Rn.
For any x, y ∈F, we have x = y = v. Therefore,
Ax = Av = Ay
This proves that Ax = Ay for every pair of points x, y ∈F.
Alternative formulation: The result can also be understood as follows: A minimal
face consists of a single point, which is uniquely determined by the active constraints. At
this vertex v, all constraints achieve specific values: for the active constraints (those in index
set I), we have aT
i v = bi, and for inactive constraints, we have aT
i v < bi. Since there is only
one point in F, the vector Av is uniquely determined, making Ax = Ay = Av for all x, y ∈F
(as they are all equal to v).
1

The points (0,0),(1,0) differ. The true Ax=Ay conclusion is not challenged. The overlay uses Set (Real x Real), proves Mathlib convexity and extremality, and proves every nonempty extreme subset is P. It additionally instantiates the exact finite-row source face definition and proves each activeFace equals P, so there is no unproved bridge from that definition to Mathlib faces. P is nonempty and not any singleton.

fields.witness:
line with lineality: every face = P

Take A = [[0,1],[0,-1]] and b = [0,0]. Then P = { (u,v) : v <= 0 and -v <= 0 } = { (u,0) : u in R }, a line. Let F = P. Under the proof's face definition, for every subset I of the two inequalities, the set {z in P : a_i^T z = b_i for all i in I} is still P, since both inequalities are tight on all of P. Hence F is a nonempty minimal face. But (0,0) and (1,0) are distinct points in F, so F is not a singleton.

scope_metadata.source_scope: General polyhedron P = {x : Ax ≤ b}, faces per the source's Definition 1 (tighten a subset I of the inequalities), minimal = containing no proper nonempty face. The witness is a line with nontrivial lineality space; the selected certificate proves it under both the source's finite-row face definition and Mathlib extreme sets.
